course.title: Constitutional, Civic & Community Literacy
course.credential_boundary: Educational civics course; not legal advice, legal training, or professional qualification.

modules.title: Constitutional Foundations
modules.essential: How constitutions organize public power, legitimacy, rights and limits.

lessons.title: Constitution, Charter and Foundational Law
lessons.focus: Distinguish a constitution from ordinary statutes, policies and customs.

lessons.title: Popular Sovereignty and Legitimate Authority
lessons.focus: Explain how political authority is justified and constrained.

lessons.title: Federalism, Separation and Shared Power
lessons.focus: Map divided authority across branches and levels of government.

modules.title: Institutions & Checks
modules.essential: How institutions distribute, constrain and coordinate governmental power.

lessons.title: Legislative Power and Representation
lessons.focus: Understand lawmaking, representation and institutional design.

lessons.title: Executive Power and Administration
lessons.focus: Distinguish executive authority, implementation and administrative power.

lessons.title: Judicial Review and Constitutional Interpretation
lessons.focus: Explain courts, review, precedent and interpretive disagreement.

modules.title: Rights, Liberties & the Bill of Rights
modules.essential: How constitutional rights limit government and structure civic claims.

lessons.title: Speech, Religion, Assembly and Petition
lessons.focus: Analyze First Amendment freedoms and their limits.

lessons.title: Privacy, Search, Due Process and Criminal Procedure
lessons.focus: Connect Fourth–Eighth Amendment protections to procedural fairness.

lessons.title: Unenumerated Rights, Reserved Powers and Constitutional Structure
lessons.focus: Interpret the Ninth and Tenth Amendments within federalism and rights debates.

modules.title: Equal Protection & Civil Rights
modules.essential: How constitutional systems address unequal treatment and exclusion.

lessons.title: Equal Protection and Legal Classification
lessons.focus: Distinguish equality principles from identical treatment.

lessons.title: Civil Rights Movements and Constitutional Change
lessons.focus: Connect legal doctrine with civic action and institutional response.

lessons.title: Rights in Practice: Access, Enforcement and Remedy
lessons.focus: Separate formal rights from practical access and enforcement.

modules.title: Law, Regulation & Public Institutions
modules.essential: How laws, rules and agencies shape everyday civic life.

lessons.title: Statutes, Regulations and Administrative Rules
lessons.focus: Distinguish major forms of public law and rulemaking.

lessons.title: Local Government and Public Services
lessons.focus: Map municipal, county and local institutional responsibilities.

lessons.title: Public Records, Meetings and Transparency
lessons.focus: Understand basic transparency, accountability and access principles.

modules.title: Elections, Representation & Participation
modules.essential: How democratic systems translate participation into public authority.

lessons.title: Voting, Districts and Representation
lessons.focus: Examine electoral structure, representation and apportionment.

lessons.title: Political Parties, Interest Groups and Civil Society
lessons.focus: Understand organized participation beyond formal government.

lessons.title: Petition, Comment, Testimony and Public Participation
lessons.focus: Practice lawful civic participation in public decision-making.

modules.title: Civil Discourse & Pluralism
modules.essential: How people disagree within a shared constitutional community.

lessons.title: Rights, Responsibilities and Civic Norms
lessons.focus: Distinguish legal rights from civic expectations and responsibilities.

lessons.title: Disagreement, Protest and Public Order
lessons.focus: Analyze tensions among expression, assembly, safety and institutional response.

lessons.title: Dialogue Across Difference
lessons.focus: Practice evidence-based disagreement without dehumanization or distortion.

modules.title: Law, Evidence & Legal Reasoning
modules.essential: How legal arguments use text, precedent, facts and interpretive principles.

lessons.title: Facts, Rules, Issues and Holdings
lessons.focus: Identify the basic structure of a legal case or dispute.

lessons.title: Precedent, Analogy and Distinguishing Cases
lessons.focus: Compare cases without treating prior decisions as mechanically identical.

lessons.title: Text, History, Purpose and Competing Interpretations
lessons.focus: Recognize multiple modes of constitutional and statutory interpretation.

modules.title: Civic Information & Media
modules.essential: How citizens verify public claims and institutional information.

lessons.title: Primary Public Sources
lessons.focus: Locate constitutions, statutes, regulations, court opinions and official records.

lessons.title: News, Commentary and Institutional Claims
lessons.focus: Separate reporting, opinion, advocacy and official statements.

lessons.title: Misinformation and Civic Verification
lessons.focus: Cross-check election, legal and policy claims before sharing or acting.

modules.title: Public Policy & Tradeoffs
modules.essential: How public decisions combine law, evidence, values, costs and competing interests.

lessons.title: Problem Definition and Stakeholders
lessons.focus: Frame a public problem without assuming a preferred solution.

lessons.title: Policy Options, Costs and Distribution
lessons.focus: Compare who benefits, who bears costs and what tradeoffs follow.

lessons.title: Implementation, Evaluation and Unintended Effects
lessons.focus: Ask whether a policy can be administered and how outcomes would be measured.

modules.title: Community, Service & Local Inquiry
modules.essential: How civic learning connects to real institutions and community needs.

lessons.title: Community Asset and Institution Mapping
lessons.focus: Identify local public institutions, civic organizations and community resources.

lessons.title: Public-Service Research
lessons.focus: Investigate a community issue using primary and local sources.

lessons.title: Volunteerism, Mutual Aid and Ethical Service
lessons.focus: Distinguish service, advocacy and paternalism while respecting community agency.

modules.title: Integrated Civic Inquiry
modules.essential: How constitutional structure, public evidence and community participation combine in civic judgment.

lessons.title: Constitutional Issue Brief
lessons.focus: Analyze a constitutional or governance question using primary sources.

lessons.title: Public Communication & Civic Proposal
lessons.focus: Prepare a concise public-facing brief or testimony.

lessons.title: Capstone Civic Defense
lessons.focus: Defend a civic conclusion while stating legal, factual and value-based uncertainties.

assessment.capstone: constitutional/public-policy issue brief + community evidence dossier + presentation/defense
